paper_metadata.title: The precipitation and effect of topologically close-packed phases in Ni-based single crystal superalloys

evidence.quote: This review seeks to comprehensively collate all the available information on TCP phases in SX superalloys based on the latest findings.
TCP phases tend to precipitate in the dendritic region after standard heat treatment, where the main TCP-forming elements Re , and W segregate.

mechanisms.name: depletion of solid solution strengthening elements

evidence.quote: The TCP phase precipitates in γ matrix and grows up by depleting the solid solution strengthening elements, such as Cr, W and Re, thus reduce the strength of γ matrix [19].
The formation of TCP phases depletes the solid solution strengthening elements causing loss of strength namely “softening effect”

For the cast material, TCP precipitates form first at the dendrite core as a result of the micro-segregation of Re, W, Mo and Cr (Fig. 1(a)) [19, 36–41], and eventually spread into interdendritic regions with the increase of exposure time.
As for the great difference of structures and compositions of the TCP and γ phase, the interface migration depends on steps, and the movement of steps reposes on diffusion of solute atoms [46–48].

mechanisms.name: γ′ volume fraction effect on γ supersaturation

evidence.quote: Two aspects were presented to explain the suppressing effect on the TCP phase nucleation: one is that the reduction of elemental partitioning behavior (k i) of the TCP-forming elements [15, 57, 115–119]; the other is the decrease of the equilibrium volume fraction of γ′ phase [15, 118].

mechanisms.name: interfacial energy reduction of μ/γ by W

evidence.section: 3.1.2 Effect of Co, Mo and W
evidence.quote: combining experimental investigations and the first principles calculations based on density functional theory (DFT) revealed that W will lower the interfacial energy of μ/γ, accelerating the nucleation of μ phase while the effects of Mo depend on the orientation relationship [46].

Several possible mechanisms for the potency of Ru as a TCP suppressant were elucidated based on experiments and simulations: (1) Ru decreases the driving force for TCP phase formation (2) Ru increases the interface energy and elastic strain energy of TCP/γ (3) Ru increases Re solubility in γ matrix (4) Ru reduces the segregation between dendrite core and interdendritic region.
It was reported that the chemical partitioning between the γ and γ′ phases were changed due to the addition of Ru, i.e., the “reverse partitioning” mechanism
the combination of experiments and DFT calculations shows that Ru can greatly increase the interfacial energy of μ/γ
Ru increases the elastic strain energy for the nucleation of the TCP phase by increasing the lattice misfit between TCP and γ phase
The formation of TCP phases depletes the solid solution strengthening elements causing loss of strength namely “softening effect”
TCP phases disrupt the rafting structure of the γ′ phase and greatly reduce the retarding effect of the γ′ phase on dislocation movement
there is a local stress field around the TCP phase, which results in a higher density of dislocations, and such dislocations can emit vacancies
